data.title: A precision line that learns before it stops
data.summary: A Rayong precision-components plant rebuilt its final assembly and inspection line around traceability and changeover speed.
data.challenge: The plant ran three product families on one line with changeovers that consumed most of a shift. Inspection results were recorded on paper, so a quality deviation could take days to trace to a machine or batch.
data.strategy: We mapped the changeover as a system rather than a sequence of tasks: tooling, recipes, quality gates, and operator decisions. The control architecture was designed around one traceable product record, with a staged migration that kept the old line running during build.
data.implementation: A new robotic assembly cell, in-line vision inspection, and a supervisor-facing OEE view were commissioned over two shutdown windows. Existing PLCs were retained where reliable; obsolete safety controls were replaced with a documented, tested architecture.
